summary: P99 latency spikes and request timeouts in prod-us-east tied to continuous batching
description:
Issue summary:
Customer AtlasPay reported intermittent p95/p99 latency spikes and request timeouts for inference calls in prod-us-east. Spikes align with increased tail latency and occasional client-observed streaming disconnects.

Impact:
- Several AtlasPay endpoints experienced 10-30s tail latencies at p99, causing timeouts in their payment orchestration flows.
- Customers observed request failures and degraded UX during peak windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool in us-east (tenant: atlaspay-prod)
- Models: redwood-7b (default), redwood-3b-quant (fallback)
- Time windows: daily spikes between 10:15-11:00 UTC and 17:40-18:20 UTC starting 2026-02-20

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Send steady stream of short chat completions (avg prompt length ~60 tokens) at ~120 QPS with occasional 10-20 request bursts.
2) Observe latency metrics and p99 values in request traces.
3) Some requests hit 30s timeout and disconnects.

Observed behavior:
- p50/p90 stable ~80-140ms, p95 elevated to ~500ms during windows, p99 spikes to 6-12s with rare >20s outliers.
- Streaming sessions report chunk gaps and eventual connection resets.
- Autoscaling did not appear to trigger additional capacity during spikes.

Expected behavior:
- Stable tail latency within SLA (p99 < 2s for this tier) and graceful autoscale or fallback to a lower-cost variant without large timeouts.

Relevant logs/traces (summarized):
- Traces show large queueing delays at the continuous-batching stage (wait times of 4-9s) before tasks enter GPU execution.
- Scheduler logs show batching window stretched beyond configured threshold when QPS fluctuates rapidly.
- No immediate OOMs or GPU errors.

Initial hypothesis: regression in continuous batching heuristics in the scheduler causing longer batching windows under bursty traffic, increasing p99 latency and timeouts.
comments: 2026-02-20 09:05 UTC - Laura Chen: Acknowledged receipt from AtlasPay. Assigned to SRE to triage. First response provided and customer asked to share traffic patterns and sample request IDs.

2026-02-20 11:02 UTC - Runtime Eng (Ravi Menon): Reproduced in a staging harness by replaying AtlasPay traffic; noticed batching window config was not honoring max-latency cutoff under burst arrival patterns. Adding temporary rate-limiter to reduce burstiness reproduced improvement.

2026-02-21 02:14 UTC - Runtime Eng (Ravi Menon): Deployed hotfix to scheduler to ensure batching window respects configured max_wait_ms when queue jitter exceeds threshold. Patch deployed to canary in us-east and monitored. Immediate reduction in queueing latency observed.
2026-02-21 10:30 UTC - Support (Laura Chen): Notified AtlasPay of canary change and asked them to verify. They reported improved behavior and no timeouts in the subsequent window.
2026-02-23 08:12 UTC - Eng Lead (Nina Gupta): Rollout completed to all dedicated pools in us-east. Post-rollout telemetry shows p99 back within SLA; closing incident. Follow-up items created.

investigation_notes: Checked telemetry: p50/p90 stable while p99 correlated with batching wait_time metric spike.

Replay in staging reproduced p99 spikes when inter-arrival jitter increased; batching window expanded beyond configured max_wait_ms due to a corner-case race in scheduler when a burst is followed by sparse arrivals.
Heap and GPU metrics show no memory pressure; throughput saturated at expected GPU levels suggesting delay before GPU execution is the cause.

Reviewed recent commits to scheduler: change in PR #872 introduced an optimization that allowed dynamic window expansion to improve throughput; regression: missing enforcement of absolute max wait time under high jitter.
Canary patch enforced max_wait_ms and added defensive checks; observed 60-80% reduction in batching wait_time and elimination of >10s tails in canary traces.
Also observed that autoscaling decision logic relied on average queue length; created issue to consider tail-aware autoscaling triggers.
Linked prior tickets SUP-4821 and SUP-8723 for historical context; similar symptoms previously attributed to batching heuristics but different root cause.
Added synthetic QPS burst tests to CI so future scheduler changes run regression harness with jittered arrival patterns.
Eng note: considered alternative mitigation of reducing max_batch_size but ruled out due to throughput cost; prioritizing correct heuristic enforcement instead.
resolution: Root cause: scheduler continuous-batching regression that allowed batching window to exceed configured max_wait_ms under bursty/jittery traffic. Fix: patched scheduler to enforce absolute max_wait_ms and added defensive checks. Deployed patch to canary 2026-02-21 02:14 UTC, monitored, then rolled out to all us-east dedicated pools by 2026-02-23 08:12 UTC. Outcome: p99 and timeout rates returned to SLA levels; AtlasPay confirmed stability.
